newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end mixed, nearbys weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end mixed, nearbys weaker.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures ended mixed in thin trade Tuesday, with much of the activity centered on the spot September contract's expiry.
"All the action was liquidation in September, which expired at 1200 (EDT) today," one trader said.
September juice finished down 3.00 cents a lb, at 114.70. Active November FCOJ settled 0.25 cent a lb weaker, at 107.20, having ranged from 109.00 to 107.00, while the rest closed up 0.05 to 0.15.
Dealers said speculative short covering lifted the market early in the session, but trade selling knocked it back down.
Fundamentally, Hurricane Hortense is likely to stay east of Florida, Weather Services Corp. said Tuesday.
"It appears there is enough of a trough developing for Hortense to miss Florida," said WSC meterologist Mike Palmerino. "It looks like it will stay east of the Bahamas."
At 1400 EDT/1500 GMT, the storm was just off the northeast coast of the Dominican Republic, moving west-northwest at about 12 mph with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph/120 kph.
